docs.text: agsrv ¶ Stateless HTTP API for remote Claude, Codex and Muse execution using their Python SDKs. Capabilities ¶ POST /v1/query : run one ephemeral agent query and receive the result as JSON, with an optional Claude message transcript. POST /v1/jobs : durable asynchronous jobs with idempotency keys; poll GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} and cancel with POST /v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel . GET /v1/info and GET /v1/agents (capabilities and cached health), plus a rate-limits route per agent ( /v1/agents/claude/rate-limits , /v1/agents/codex/rate-limits , /v1/agents/muse/rate-limits ). GET /health needs no authentication. Bearer-token authentication, workspace confinement, per-agent concurrency limits, and a global timeout cap. No sessions, resume, or server-side conversation state, and no streaming endpoint: every request is one ephemeral run. Development ¶ uv sync uv run uvicorn agsrv.main:app --host 127 .0.0.1 --port 8000 Since 0.4.0 the last command needs AGSRV_TMP_STAGING_DIRS set first — see Deployment (Local development). API reference Deployment Licensed under AGPL-3.0-only.

docs.text: API Reference ¶ agsrv exposes a stateless REST API around the Claude, Codex and Muse SDKs: GET /health : readiness probe (no auth). GET /v1/info : server defaults and limits. GET /v1/agents : agent availability and capabilities. GET /v1/agents/claude/rate-limits : Claude subscription quota. GET /v1/agents/codex/rate-limits : Codex account limits. GET /v1/agents/muse/rate-limits : Muse last-observed subscription usage. POST /v1/query : one agent run, JSON result with an optional Claude transcript. POST /v1/jobs : submit a durable asynchronous job (202). GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} : poll a job's status and terminal result. POST /v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel : request cancellation. REST API Deployment

docs.text: Deployment ¶ Local development ¶ Since 0.4.0 the server refuses to start without a staging directory for the workspace root's mount (see AGSRV_TMP_STAGING_DIRS in the README), even for local development. Provision one outside the workspace root and point the setting at it: uv sync mkdir -p ~/.agsrv-stage && chmod 700 ~/.agsrv-stage AGSRV_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED = true \ AGSRV_TMP_STAGING_DIRS = " $PWD = $HOME /.agsrv-stage" \ uv run uvicorn agsrv.main:app --host 127 .0.0.1 --port 8000 The key (here $PWD ) must contain the workspace root; if you set AGSRV_WORKSPACE_ROOT to something else, use that value (or an ancestor of it) as the key instead. Remote server ¶ Install dependencies on the server: git clone https://github.com/dceoy/agsrv.git /opt/agsrv cd /opt/agsrv && uv sync --no-dev Authenticate Claude on the server. The SDK spawns the Claude Code CLI, so either set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment file below, or log in once with claude as the user that runs the service. Provision a staging directory (mandatory since 0.4.0): service-owned, mode 0700 , outside the workspace root, on the same mount as it — for example install -d -m 700 -o agsrv /var/lib/agsrv/stage . Without it the server fails to start. Create /etc/agsrv.env (mode 0600 ): AGSRV_API_KEY = <long random secret, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32 > AGSRV_WORKSPACE_ROOT = /srv/workspaces AGSRV_TMP_STAGING_DIRS = /srv/workspaces = /var/lib/agsrv/stage ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = sk-ant-... Run uvicorn on loopback or a private interface, and expose it only through TLS (a reverse proxy) or a private network such as Tailscale or an SSH tunnel ( ssh -L 8000:127.0.0.1:8000 server ). Run it as an unprivileged user that owns only the workspace directory (and the staging directory above). Workspace confinement limits the starting cwd , not what Bash can reach. The agent inherits this environment file, so a run can read AGSRV_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from its own environment — the API key is effectively a shell as this user (see the README security model). The concurrency limit is per process: running uvicorn with --workers N multiplies AGSRV_MAX_CONCURRENCY by N. The durable job queue currently requires exactly one worker for a database. Store AGSRV_JOBS_DB_PATH on persistent storage with restricted permissions. systemd unit ¶ [Unit] Description = agsrv After = network-online.target [Service] User = agsrv WorkingDirectory = /opt/agsrv EnvironmentFile = /etc/agsrv.env ExecStart = /opt/agsrv/.venv/bin/uvicorn agsrv.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 Restart = on-failure NoNewPrivileges = true [Install] WantedBy = multi-user.target Bash sandbox (enabled by default) ¶ Claude runs use the fail-closed CLI Bash sandbox by default. Explicit sandbox: false is reserved for host-control tasks that must bypass it. Prerequisites on the host: bwrap (bubblewrap), socat , and rg (ripgrep). Sandboxed runs are pinned to the CLI bundled with the installed claude-agent-sdk ( cli_path ), never any claude on PATH ; if the bundled executable is missing or not executable the request fails (503). Its version decides how sandbox settings are interpreted, so redo the probe below after every SDK update. Sandboxed requests are rejected (403) when the effective permission mode is auto or bypassPermissions , and when the working directory overlaps ~/.cache (for example a workspace root equal to the service home with no cwd ). Keep AGSRV_WORKSPACE_ROOT away from the service home, or ensure clients send a cwd below a project directory. ~/.cache/agsrv-sandbox is created with mode 0700 on first use; it must be a real directory owned by the service user (symlinks are rejected). Its mode is set to and verified as exactly 0700, and ~/.cache itself must not be group- or other-writable; otherwise requests fail with 503. The sandbox is fail-closed. On Ubuntu releases that ship the bwrap-userns-restrict AppArmor profile, the sandbox's seccomp helper cannot start, so sandbox: true requests fail until the host policy is adjusted (for example with a dedicated, AppArmor-profiled copy of bwrap placed first on the service PATH ). Do not weaken this by disabling the sandbox checks. Before deployment, run an acceptance probe with the default (sandboxed) run: Verify AGSRV_SANDBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS permits only required hosts. Run a request without a sandbox field: echo ok succeeds; writes outside the working directory and the sandbox cache are denied; secret directories such as ~/.ssh are unreadable; env shows no AGSRV_API_KEY ; curl to a non-allow-listed host is denied; and systemctl --user status fails. Clients must never retry a failed default sandbox request with sandbox: false ; that would reintroduce fail-open behaviour. Durable jobs ¶ Use the same long-lived API key on replacement Muse VMs and submit jobs with a stable Idempotency-Key . Poll GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} without holding open a connection. Back up the SQLite WAL database (including its WAL file) and avoid multi-worker uvicorn: an exclusive sibling lock file rejects concurrent processes sharing the database. Synchronous queries share the same workspace lease as queued jobs. Jobs are in-process: a server restart marks uncompleted jobs interrupted and never retries them automatically. Default completed-job retention is 24 hours. All holders of the same bearer token can inspect jobs created with that token; do not share credentials across untrusted tenants. Client smoke test ¶ From the client machine (here via an SSH tunnel on localhost:8000 ): curl -sS http://localhost:8000/health curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/info -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGSRV_API_KEY " curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGSRV_API_KEY " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"agent": "claude", "prompt": "Reply with the single word: pong", "max_turns": 1}' A 200 response with "result": "pong" confirms authentication, Claude credentials, and the SDK/CLI path all work.

docs.text: REST API ¶ All /v1/* endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <AGSRV_API_KEY> . FastAPI also serves /docs and /openapi.json . Statelessness contract ¶ Every request is one ephemeral Claude, Codex or Muse run. The server keeps no sessions and offers no resume, continue, or fork. The session_id in responses is informational only and cannot be sent back: request bodies with unknown fields (such as resume or session_id ) are rejected with 422 . To continue work, include the needed context in the next prompt. Claude runs are hermetic. CLI session persistence is disabled, so the CLI writes no resumable transcript, and host and project settings are not loaded ( setting_sources is empty): hooks, MCP servers, and permission rules from the host's or the workspace's .claude/settings.json never enter a run. Auto memory is disabled ( CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 ), and MCP configuration is strict and isolated. Managed policy settings and ~/.claude.json still load. What persists after a run is only what the agent itself writes — files in the workspace and ordinary CLI bookkeeping under ~/.claude . GET /health ¶ No authentication. { "status" : "ok" } GET /v1/info ¶ { "version" : "0.4.0" , "stateless" : true , "default_model" : null , "workspace_root" : "/srv/workspaces" , "default_permission_mode" : "acceptEdits" , "default_allowed_tools" : [ "Read" , "Write" , "Edit" , "Bash" , "Glob" , "Grep" ], "max_concurrency" : 4 , "auth_required" : true , "sandbox_allowed_domains" : [ "github.com" , "api.github.com" , "codeload.github.com" , "uploads.github.com" , "raw.githubusercontent.com" , "objects.githubusercontent.com" , "release-assets.githubusercontent.com" , "pypi.org" , "files.pythonhosted.org" , "registry.npmjs.org" ] } POST /v1/query ¶ Claude request ( agent and prompt are required): { "agent" : "claude" , "prompt" : "List the Python files" , "model" : null , "cwd" : "myproject" , "allowed_tools" : [ "Read" , "Glob" ], "permission_mode" : "default" , "max_turns" : 5 , "effort" : "low" , "timeout_seconds" : 300 , "include_messages" : true , "sandbox" : true } include_messages : when false , the response omits the transcript ( messages is [] ); intended for result-only clients. sandbox : defaults to true , running Bash inside the fail-closed CLI sandbox. Only explicit false opts out for host-control operations. Never retry a failed sandboxed run with sandbox: false . Requests are rejected with 403 if the effective permission mode (request value, else the server default) is auto or bypassPermissions (incompatible with the sandbox's egress allow-list), or if the resolved cwd overlaps the shared cache: it is ~/.cache , an ancestor of it (such as the service home directory), or inside ~/.cache outside ~/.cache/agsrv-sandbox . If sandbox prerequisites cannot be established (unknown home, unusable cache directory, missing bundled CLI) the response is 503. cwd : relative to AGSRV_WORKSPACE_ROOT , or absolute inside it. allowed_tools : an auto-approve list, not a restriction. It names tools the run may use without a permission decision; it does not remove other tools, and file edits are still approved under acceptEdits . When omitted, the server default ( AGSRV_ALLOWED_TOOLS ) applies — a default, not a ceiling. permission_mode : default , acceptEdits , plan , bypassPermissions (always rejected with 403), dontAsk , auto . max_turns : 1–1000. timeout_seconds must be > 0; timeout_seconds may not exceed AGSRV_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS . If a Claude client disconnects, the run is promptly cancelled and its concurrency slot is freed. The server internally answers 499 without logging an error; the response is not delivered to the disconnected client. Response: { "agent" : "claude" , "result" : "There are 3 Python files." , "session_id" : "0b0e..." , "model" : "..." , "subtype" : "success" , "is_error" : false , "num_turns" : 2 , "duration_ms" : 4210 , "duration_api_ms" : 3900 , "total_cost_usd" : 0.0123 , "usage" : { "input_tokens" : 100 , "output_tokens" : 40 }, "stop_reason" : "end_turn" , "messages" : [ { "type" : "system" , "subtype" : "init" , "data" : {} }, { "type" : "assistant" , "model" : "..." , "content" : [ { "type" : "thinking" , "thinking" : "..." , "signature" : "..." }, { "type" : "tool_use" , "id" : "t1" , "name" : "Glob" , "input" : { "pattern" : "*.py" } } ], "error" : null , "usage" : null , "stop_reason" : null , "session_id" : null , "uuid" : null }, { "type" : "user" , "content" : [ { "type" : "tool_result" , "tool_use_id" : "t1" , "content" : "a.py" , "is_error" : false } ], "uuid" : null , "parent_tool_use_id" : null }, { "type" : "result" , "subtype" : "success" , "is_error" : false , "result" : "..." , "session_id" : "0b0e..." , "num_turns" : 2 , "duration_ms" : 4210 , "duration_api_ms" : 3900 , "total_cost_usd" : 0.0123 , "usage" : null , "stop_reason" : "end_turn" , "errors" : null } ] } The top-level model is the model reported by the run's assistant messages (the last one wins) and is null when the run produced no assistant message, so clients can verify the model that actually ran without parsing the transcript. An agent-level failure ( is_error: true , e.g. subtype: "error_max_turns" ) is still HTTP 200 . Message types not listed above are emitted as {"type": "<snake_case_class>", "data": {...}} . Codex requests ¶ { "agent" : "codex" , "prompt" : "Summarize this project" , "cwd" : "." , "model" : null , "effort" : "high" , "timeout_seconds" : 300 , "include_messages" : false , "options" : { "sandbox" : "read-only" , "network_access" : false } } options.sandbox is read-only (default) or workspace-write ; network_access defaults to false . cwd is confined to the same workspace root as Claude. include_messages is accepted for consistency; Codex returns a turn summary rather than a transcript. The response contains agent , result , model , is_error , duration_ms , usage , and backend with the turn ID, status and executed commands. The model comes from thread metadata, or is null when unavailable. Codex threads use ephemeral=true (D1) and approval policy never , with an additional handler that declines all approval requests. Rate limits use the typed account/rateLimits/read request (D2). For network access the adapter uses an explicit low-level sandbox policy; otherwise it uses SDK presets (D3). Set AGSRV_CODEX_ENABLED (default true ), AGSRV_CODEX_BIN (optional SDK binary override), and AGSRV_CODEX_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2 ). A disabled or unavailable backend returns 503 without affecting Claude. Muse requests ¶ { "agent" : "muse" , "prompt" : "Summarize this project" , "cwd" : "." , "model" : null , "effort" : "high" , "timeout_seconds" : 300 , "include_messages" : false } effort is one of none , minimal , low , medium , high , xhigh , max , ultra . Muse uses muse serve --no-session-log --contributor-mode off with a fixed sandbox posture (never --disable-sandbox or --trust-workspace ), a deny-all on_approval handler and approval mode onRequest . Sessions are memory-only; if client.durability is not ephemeral the backend fails closed and GET /v1/agents reports unhealthy. include_messages is accepted for parity but no transcript is returned in v1. The backend is disabled by default ( AGSRV_MUSE_ENABLED=false ) and requires a logged-in muse host matching the SDK version ( muse-code-sdk==1.4.24 with muse 1.4.24 ); upgrade them together. There is no streaming variant for any agent; all queries are request/response. GET /v1/agents ¶ Returns claude , codex and muse objects with enabled , healthy , default_model , and supports flags for sandbox , network_access , rate_limits , and streaming . Claude and Codex health probes are cached for approximately 30 seconds. Muse initialization follows the same cached (~30s) probe pattern, checking ephemeral durability and sandbox availability. Claude uses the local /usage command, without consuming tokens or allowance. Claude is healthy when the CLI is spawnable, the ephemeral /usage run does not return an error result, and the bundled CLI's auth status reports loggedIn: true . The probe never uses the sandbox. This proves a configured, spawnable CLI whose /usage run succeeds; it does not prove the credential is still valid server-side (an expired or revoked token can pass until a real turn runs). While the Claude concurrency slot is busy, this endpoint returns the last cached health value (even if expired) and never responds 429 because of the Claude probe. The Codex entry is unaffected: with Codex enabled and its concurrency slot busy and its cached probe has expired, this endpoint can still respond 429. The same applies to the Muse entry when Muse is enabled, its slot is busy, and its cached probe has expired. GET /v1/agents/claude/rate-limits ¶ Runs the local Claude CLI's /usage command and returns the normalized rate-limit windows together with the raw text. If the output cannot be parsed, available is false. The /usage command consumes no tokens or subscription allowance. The route spawns a Claude child process, so it receives the same admission, disk-space preflight and per-turn TMPDIR handling as a query — unlike the Codex route below, which starts no workspace turn. GET /v1/agents/muse/rate-limits ¶ Returns the host's last-observed subscription usage without a model call or a session. five_hour and seven_day contain used_percent and an ISO 8601 resets_at , or null when unavailable. raw and backend preserve the SDK payload; fetched_at is the read time. A fresh host may have no cached usage, in which case available is false. Disabled or unavailable Muse returns 503; backend failures return 502 and timeouts return 504. GET /v1/agents/codex/rate-limits ¶ Returns plan , primary and secondary windows ( used_percent and resets_at ), reached_type , reset_credits , and the raw SDK payload in backend . Missing windows are null. Durable asynchronous jobs ¶ POST /v1/jobs accepts the same discriminated Claude/Codex/Muse JSON body as /v1/query . Unlike synchronous queries, the server owns execution after the 202 response and continues across HTTP disconnects. Example: POST /v1/jobs Authorization: Bearer <AGSRV_API_KEY> Idempotency-Key: vm-task-123 Content-Type: application/json {"agent":"claude","prompt":"Analyze the repository","cwd":"myproject"} Returns 202: {"job_id":"<opaque UUID>","status_url":"/v1/jobs/<id>"} . The optional Idempotency-Key (1–128 printable ASCII chars) is scoped to the bearer principal. Identical validated requests reuse the job ID even on retries after a VM is destroyed. A conflicting payload returns 409; once the terminal record expires, key reuse can create a new job. GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} returns job_id , agent , status , created_at , started_at , finished_at , result , and error . Statuses are queued , running , succeeded , failed , cancelled , or interrupted . result contains the normalized Claude, Codex or Muse response only on completion. Agent-level errors become failed with a retained result; transport failures and deadlines have sanitized error.code values. POST /v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel is idempotent: queued jobs stop immediately, running jobs remain nonterminal until their child processes are cleaned up. The job database is SQLite WAL; it must be on durable storage accessible to a single uvicorn worker . An exclusive lock file alongside the database prevents concurrent workers or overlapping instances from taking ownership. The default path is ~/.local/state/agsrv/jobs.sqlite3 (overridden by AGSRV_JOBS_DB_PATH ). Nonterminal jobs are limited by AGSRV_JOBS_MAX_PENDING=32 , canonical requests by AGSRV_JOBS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES=65536 , stored results by AGSRV_JOBS_MAX_RESULT_BYTES=1048576 ; saturation gives 429 and Retry-After: 5 . Terminal jobs and idempotency keys are retained for AGSRV_JOBS_RETENTION_SECONDS=86400 (24 hours). Garbage collection is performed during API access. Synchronous queries and jobs targeting overlapping workspaces cannot execute concurrently. When a result exceeds the configured cap, message history is omitted with messages_truncated: true while keeping the final answer. If the core result is still oversized, a minimal summary is stored with result_truncated: true so the original execution outcome is not misreported. Extremely small caps that cannot fit this summary result in failed / result_too_large . The bearer token is the caller identity: all clients sharing the same API key can read the same jobs ; use separate server credentials and instances if isolation between clients is needed. No raw internal errors or credentials are included in job status. The in-process scheduler does not guarantee completion across a server restart . On restart both queued and running jobs become interrupted without replaying side effects; completed results remain until expiry. The old SSE stream endpoint is deliberately removed. Errors ¶ Status Meaning 400 cwd missing or not a directory; timeout_seconds above server max 401 Missing or incorrect bearer token 403 cwd outside workspace root; bypassPermissions always forbidden; with an egress-expanding permission mode ( auto , bypassPermissions ), or with a cwd overlapping the shared cache ( ~/.cache outside ~/.cache/agsrv-sandbox , or an ancestor such as the home directory) 409 Idempotency-Key reused with a different job payload 413 Durable job payload too large 404 Job not found or not authorized for this caller 422 Invalid body (empty prompt, unknown/stateful fields, bad ranges) 429 Concurrency or pending-job capacity reached (jobs include Retry-After) 502 SDK/CLI failure, or the run ended without a result message 503 AGSRV_API_KEY not configured and unauthenticated access not allowed; sandbox prerequisites unavailable; Claude, Codex or Muse disabled/unavailable; or the turn could not be prepared — the disk-space preflight found free space on /tmp , the workspace root or the working directory below its threshold; no staging directory is configured for the working directory's mount; the working directory failed acceptance revalidation (a missing component, a symlink, or a substituted directory); or the per-turn directory could not be created (for example an owner-clearing umask , or EXDEV ) 504 Run exceeded its timeout Errors use FastAPI's {"detail": "..."} body.

docs.text: All /v1/* endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <AGSRV_API_KEY> . FastAPI also serves /docs and /openapi.json .
docs.title: REST API

docs.text: Every request is one ephemeral Claude, Codex or Muse run. The server keeps no sessions and offers no resume, continue, or fork. The session_id in responses is informational only and cannot be sent back: request bodies with unknown fields (such as resume or session_id ) are rejected with 422 . To continue work, include the needed context in the next prompt. Claude runs are hermetic. CLI session persistence is disabled, so the CLI writes no resumable transcript, and host and project settings are not loaded ( setting_sources is empty): hooks, MCP servers, and permission rules from the host's or the workspace's .claude/settings.json never enter a run. Auto memory is disabled ( CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 ), and MCP configuration is strict and isolated. Managed policy settings and ~/.claude.json still load. What persists after a run is only what the agent itself writes — files in the workspace and ordinary CLI bookkeeping under ~/.claude .
docs.title: Statelessness contract

docs.text: No authentication. { "status" : "ok" }

docs.text: Claude request ( agent and prompt are required): { "agent" : "claude" , "prompt" : "List the Python files" , "model" : null , "cwd" : "myproject" , "allowed_tools" : [ "Read" , "Glob" ], "permission_mode" : "default" , "max_turns" : 5 , "effort" : "low" , "timeout_seconds" : 300 , "include_messages" : true , "sandbox" : true } include_messages : when false , the response omits the transcript ( messages is [] ); intended for result-only clients. sandbox : defaults to true , running Bash inside the fail-closed CLI sandbox. Only explicit false opts out for host-control operations. Never retry a failed sandboxed run with sandbox: false . Requests are rejected with 403 if the effective permission mode (request value, else the server default) is auto or bypassPermissions (incompatible with the sandbox's egress allow-list), or if the resolved cwd overlaps the shared cache: it is ~/.cache , an ancestor of it (such as the service home directory), or inside ~/.cache outside ~/.cache/agsrv-sandbox . If sandbox prerequisites cannot be established (unknown home, unusable cache directory, missing bundled CLI) the response is 503. cwd : relative to AGSRV_WORKSPACE_ROOT , or absolute inside it. allowed_tools : an auto-approve list, not a restriction. It names tools the run may use without a permission decision; it does not remove other tools, and file edits are still approved under acceptEdits . When omitted, the server default ( AGSRV_ALLOWED_TOOLS ) applies — a default, not a ceiling. permission_mode : default , acceptEdits , plan , bypassPermissions (always rejected with 403), dontAsk , auto . max_turns : 1–1000. timeout_seconds must be > 0; timeout_seconds may not exceed AGSRV_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS . If a Claude client disconnects, the run is promptly cancelled and its concurrency slot is freed. The server internally answers 499 without logging an error; the response is not delivered to the disconnected client. Response: { "agent" : "claude" , "result" : "There are 3 Python files." , "session_id" : "0b0e..." , "model" : "..." , "subtype" : "success" , "is_error" : false , "num_turns" : 2 , "duration_ms" : 4210 , "duration_api_ms" : 3900 , "total_cost_usd" : 0.0123 , "usage" : { "input_tokens" : 100 , "output_tokens" : 40 }, "stop_reason" : "end_turn" , "messages" : [ { "type" : "system" , "subtype" : "init" , "data" : {} }, { "type" : "assistant" , "model" : "..." , "content" : [ { "type" : "thinking" , "thinking" : "..." , "signature" : "..." }, { "type" : "tool_use" , "id" : "t1" , "name" : "Glob" , "input" : { "pattern" : "*.py" } } ], "error" : null , "usage" : null , "stop_reason" : null , "session_id" : null , "uuid" : null }, { "type" : "user" , "content" : [ { "type" : "tool_result" , "tool_use_id" : "t1" , "content" : "a.py" , "is_error" : false } ], "uuid" : null , "parent_tool_use_id" : null }, { "type" : "result" , "subtype" : "success" , "is_error" : false , "result" : "..." , "session_id" : "0b0e..." , "num_turns" : 2 , "duration_ms" : 4210 , "duration_api_ms" : 3900 , "total_cost_usd" : 0.0123 , "usage" : null , "stop_reason" : "end_turn" , "errors" : null } ] } The top-level model is the model reported by the run's assistant messages (the last one wins) and is null when the run produced no assistant message, so clients can verify the model that actually ran without parsing the transcript. An agent-level failure ( is_error: true , e.g. subtype: "error_max_turns" ) is still HTTP 200 . Message types not listed above are emitted as {"type": "<snake_case_class>", "data": {...}} .

docs.text: { "agent" : "codex" , "prompt" : "Summarize this project" , "cwd" : "." , "model" : null , "effort" : "high" , "timeout_seconds" : 300 , "include_messages" : false , "options" : { "sandbox" : "read-only" , "network_access" : false } } options.sandbox is read-only (default) or workspace-write ; network_access defaults to false . cwd is confined to the same workspace root as Claude. include_messages is accepted for consistency; Codex returns a turn summary rather than a transcript. The response contains agent , result , model , is_error , duration_ms , usage , and backend with the turn ID, status and executed commands. The model comes from thread metadata, or is null when unavailable. Codex threads use ephemeral=true (D1) and approval policy never , with an additional handler that declines all approval requests. Rate limits use the typed account/rateLimits/read request (D2). For network access the adapter uses an explicit low-level sandbox policy; otherwise it uses SDK presets (D3). Set AGSRV_CODEX_ENABLED (default true ), AGSRV_CODEX_BIN (optional SDK binary override), and AGSRV_CODEX_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2 ). A disabled or unavailable backend returns 503 without affecting Claude.
docs.title: Codex requests

docs.text: { "agent" : "muse" , "prompt" : "Summarize this project" , "cwd" : "." , "model" : null , "effort" : "high" , "timeout_seconds" : 300 , "include_messages" : false } effort is one of none , minimal , low , medium , high , xhigh , max , ultra . Muse uses muse serve --no-session-log --contributor-mode off with a fixed sandbox posture (never --disable-sandbox or --trust-workspace ), a deny-all on_approval handler and approval mode onRequest . Sessions are memory-only; if client.durability is not ephemeral the backend fails closed and GET /v1/agents reports unhealthy. include_messages is accepted for parity but no transcript is returned in v1. The backend is disabled by default ( AGSRV_MUSE_ENABLED=false ) and requires a logged-in muse host matching the SDK version ( muse-code-sdk==1.4.24 with muse 1.4.24 ); upgrade them together. There is no streaming variant for any agent; all queries are request/response.
docs.title: Muse requests

docs.text: Returns claude , codex and muse objects with enabled , healthy , default_model , and supports flags for sandbox , network_access , rate_limits , and streaming . Claude and Codex health probes are cached for approximately 30 seconds. Muse initialization follows the same cached (~30s) probe pattern, checking ephemeral durability and sandbox availability. Claude uses the local /usage command, without consuming tokens or allowance. Claude is healthy when the CLI is spawnable, the ephemeral /usage run does not return an error result, and the bundled CLI's auth status reports loggedIn: true . The probe never uses the sandbox. This proves a configured, spawnable CLI whose /usage run succeeds; it does not prove the credential is still valid server-side (an expired or revoked token can pass until a real turn runs). While the Claude concurrency slot is busy, this endpoint returns the last cached health value (even if expired) and never responds 429 because of the Claude probe. The Codex entry is unaffected: with Codex enabled and its concurrency slot busy and its cached probe has expired, this endpoint can still respond 429. The same applies to the Muse entry when Muse is enabled, its slot is busy, and its cached probe has expired.
docs.title: GET /v1/agents

docs.text: Runs the local Claude CLI's /usage command and returns the normalized rate-limit windows together with the raw text. If the output cannot be parsed, available is false. The /usage command consumes no tokens or subscription allowance. The route spawns a Claude child process, so it receives the same admission, disk-space preflight and per-turn TMPDIR handling as a query — unlike the Codex route below, which starts no workspace turn.
docs.title: GET /v1/agents/claude/rate-limits

docs.text: Returns the host's last-observed subscription usage without a model call or a session. five_hour and seven_day contain used_percent and an ISO 8601 resets_at , or null when unavailable. raw and backend preserve the SDK payload; fetched_at is the read time. A fresh host may have no cached usage, in which case available is false. Disabled or unavailable Muse returns 503; backend failures return 502 and timeouts return 504.
docs.title: GET /v1/agents/muse/rate-limits

docs.text: Returns plan , primary and secondary windows ( used_percent and resets_at ), reached_type , reset_credits , and the raw SDK payload in backend . Missing windows are null.
docs.title: GET /v1/agents/codex/rate-limits

docs.text: POST /v1/jobs accepts the same discriminated Claude/Codex/Muse JSON body as /v1/query . Unlike synchronous queries, the server owns execution after the 202 response and continues across HTTP disconnects. Example: POST /v1/jobs Authorization: Bearer <AGSRV_API_KEY> Idempotency-Key: vm-task-123 Content-Type: application/json {"agent":"claude","prompt":"Analyze the repository","cwd":"myproject"} Returns 202: {"job_id":"<opaque UUID>","status_url":"/v1/jobs/<id>"} . The optional Idempotency-Key (1–128 printable ASCII chars) is scoped to the bearer principal. Identical validated requests reuse the job ID even on retries after a VM is destroyed. A conflicting payload returns 409; once the terminal record expires, key reuse can create a new job. GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} returns job_id , agent , status , created_at , started_at , finished_at , result , and error . Statuses are queued , running , succeeded , failed , cancelled , or interrupted . result contains the normalized Claude, Codex or Muse response only on completion. Agent-level errors become failed with a retained result; transport failures and deadlines have sanitized error.code values. POST /v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel is idempotent: queued jobs stop immediately, running jobs remain nonterminal until their child processes are cleaned up. The job database is SQLite WAL; it must be on durable storage accessible to a single uvicorn worker . An exclusive lock file alongside the database prevents concurrent workers or overlapping instances from taking ownership. The default path is ~/.local/state/agsrv/jobs.sqlite3 (overridden by AGSRV_JOBS_DB_PATH ). Nonterminal jobs are limited by AGSRV_JOBS_MAX_PENDING=32 , canonical requests by AGSRV_JOBS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES=65536 , stored results by AGSRV_JOBS_MAX_RESULT_BYTES=1048576 ; saturation gives 429 and Retry-After: 5 . Terminal jobs and idempotency keys are retained for AGSRV_JOBS_RETENTION_SECONDS=86400 (24 hours). Garbage collection is performed during API access. Synchronous queries and jobs targeting overlapping workspaces cannot execute concurrently. When a result exceeds the configured cap, message history is omitted with messages_truncated: true while keeping the final answer. If the core result is still oversized, a minimal summary is stored with result_truncated: true so the original execution outcome is not misreported. Extremely small caps that cannot fit this summary result in failed / result_too_large . The bearer token is the caller identity: all clients sharing the same API key can read the same jobs ; use separate server credentials and instances if isolation between clients is needed. No raw internal errors or credentials are included in job status. The in-process scheduler does not guarantee completion across a server restart . On restart both queued and running jobs become interrupted without replaying side effects; completed results remain until expiry. The old SSE stream endpoint is deliberately removed.
